textbookText: Harmful Effects: Fungi are directly or indirectly harmful to the human beings in various ways. They may cause diseases of plants, human beings, animals; spoilage of food, etc.

1. Plant diseases: Fungi cause several diseases to varieties of economic value plants. Such as, club root disease in cabbage, wart disease in potato, damping off disease in various seedlings, red rots in sugarcane etc.

2. Rotting of fruit and food: Poor storage of crops and fruits leads to the growth of fungi causing high economic losses like Penicillium species causes green rot on fruit, Aspergillus species cause black rot in fruit, Aspergillus flavus cause green rot in grains, etc. Fungi spoil the vegetables, dairy products, meat etc.

3. Human and animal diseases: Certain fungi are parasite on human and animals causing infection of skin, hair or nails. Aquatic fungi live as parasite on egg and gills of fishes causing severe damage to them.

4. Damage of clothes: Fungi can grow on wet clothes and shoes hence damage them. Clothes made from natural fibers such as cotton, wool, silk are more susceptible than those made from synthetic fibres.
5. Damage of paper and wood: Many fungi destroy the paper of books and newspapers in moist conditions. The species of Polyporus cause the damage and decay the timber wood.
6. Mushroom poisoning: Poisonous mushroom causes the different types of health hazards in human beings like
diarrhea, vomiting, gastric disturbance and even death of person.
